name: Contour Atlas
brief: The page is a bound atlas sheet. A coordinate frame runs around the viewport edge (A–H across the top, 1–12 down the side), and every section is a numbered map sheet with a neat line, scale bar and north arrow in the corner. The hero is a full-bleed contour terrain in hairline strokes of --c-primary on a paper-cream ground, with the headline set like a mountain-range label: italic, widely letterspaced, curving along a path. Product categories are a legend table of symbol, name and count, and products are plotted as numbered survey points on a grid of map tiles; each card carries a grid reference such as 'C4' that the nav search also understands. Contact is a gazetteer entry with lat/long and a CSS-drawn locator inset. The mood is calm, precise and outdoorsy. Any brand colour reads as an elevation tint because all other ink is a warm sepia.
type: Display: 'Alegreya' 800 for headlines and italic 400 with 0.3em tracking for 'water-style' labels set on SVG textPath; labels 'Alegreya Sans SC' 500; body 'Alegreya Sans' 400.
signature: Live contour terrain: a canvas computes a 2D simplex-noise heightfield and draws isolines with marching squares (about 14 levels, redrawn at 30fps). The pointer acts as a Gaussian 'hill' added to the heightfield, so contour lines bunch and bend around the cursor. Hovering a product point raises a sharp peak at its coordinates and briefly highlights that elevation band in --c-primary. Under prefers-reduced-motion it renders a single static frame.
source: Topographic survey maps and 19th-century atlas plates

name: Departure Board
brief: The homepage is a station concourse after dark: a near-black board housing on a charcoal ground, lit by a single --c-primary status lamp. The hero is a giant board where the brand promise sits in the 'destination' column. Products are listed as departures: 'time' is the price, 'destination' is the product name, 'platform' is the category, and the status column shows In stock, Last few or Delayed (backorder) in the accent colour. Categories are platform signs across a horizontal concourse strip, and 'Now boarding' is the featured-product CTA. Section headers are hanging enamel signs with a numbered platform circle. Contact is an information desk with opening hours set as a timetable. The mood is loud, nocturnal and mechanical.
type: Display: 'Big Shoulders Display' 800 uppercase for signage and section titles; flap characters 'Azeret Mono' 600 in fixed-width cells; body 'Hanken Grotesk' 400/500.
signature: Real split-flap characters: each character is a cell made of two halves (top and bottom div) with a hinged flap that rotates rotateX(-180deg) in 60ms steps. When a row enters view or a filter changes, every cell cycles through the character set from its current glyph to its target glyph, with a random 0–200ms start per cell, then settles. An optional tiny clack is synthesised with WebAudio noise bursts, muted by default. Filtering categories re-flaps the whole board instead of re-rendering the grid.
source: Mechanical split-flap timetable boards in railway halls

name: Inventory Screen
brief: The site is a game's equipment screen. The hero is a split panel: the left side shows a 'character' silhouette built from CSS shapes with equip slots (head, hands, body, feet, bag), and the right side shows the headline and a 'Start' CTA. The catalog is a dense square-slot grid with beveled frames; rarity tiers (common, rare, epic, legendary) map to tints of --c-primary and --c-accent so they work with any brand colour. Each item opens a stat card with bars for weight, durability and price, plus a flavour-text line in italics. The nav is a tab strip (Gear, Quests = services, Map = contact, Bag = cart) with keyboard hints like [Q] [E]. Backgrounds are dark slate with a faint pixel-dither gradient, and the mood is playful and dark.
type: Display: 'Pixelify Sans' 700 for tabs, headings and numbers only; body 'Atkinson Hyperlegible' 400/700 for everything readable, including stat cards.
signature: Drag-to-equip: product slots are draggable (pointer events, with a ghost image that snaps to an 8px grid). Dropping an item on a matching character slot or the Bag slot animates it into place with a 3-frame 'pop' (scale 1.2 → 0.9 → 1) and adds it to a localStorage cart. The full grid is also navigable with arrow keys and a glowing selection cursor; Enter equips. A tooltip stat card follows the cursor or selection and clamps to the viewport.
source: Role-playing game inventory and loadout interfaces

name: Score Sheet
brief: Every page is a printed score on warm ivory. Five-line staves form the baseline grid, sections are 'movements' with tempo markings (I. Allegro — Our shop, II. Andante — Collection), and bar lines divide content columns. The hero places the headline across a grand staff with a large clef-like brand monogram, and the CTA reads as a fermata-marked button. Products sit as 'notes' along the staves: each card hangs from the line at a height set by its price, with stems and ledger lines drawn in SVG, and opens into a clean detail card. Dynamics (pp, mf, ff) label stock levels and rehearsal letters (A, B, C) act as anchor links in the nav. The mood is calm, literate and light, with --c-primary used only for the playhead and the active notes.
type: Display: 'Petrona' 900 for movement titles and 300 italic for tempo and dynamics marks; body 'Inter Tight' 400 at modest sizes; rehearsal letters set in boxed 'Petrona' 700.
signature: Playhead performance: a 'Play' button starts a vertical playhead (a --c-primary line) that sweeps across the visible stave at a set tempo using requestAnimationFrame. As it crosses each product note, the note lights up, the card lifts slightly, and WebAudio plays a soft sine-plus-triangle tone whose pitch maps to the note's height. The playhead pauses on hover so the user can click the active product. It is silent until the user presses Play.

name: Specimen Cabinet
brief: The site is a naturalist's collection. The layout is a cabinet of shallow drawers stacked down the page, each with a brass-coloured label frame (category name, drawer number and item count). The hero is a single plate: an oversized product shot pinned at the centre of white board, surrounded by a hairline numbered key with the brand story as the plate caption. Products are 'specimens' on a strict ruled grid: each sits in a ruled cell with a catalogue number, a Latin-style italic sub-name, an origin and a weight, like a museum label. Fine dotted rules, a plate border and a faint foxed-paper tone make up the texture. The mood is severe, quiet and scholarly; --c-primary appears only in the label tabs and the catalogue numbers.
type: Display: 'Libre Caslon Display' 400 large with optical tightness for plate titles; body 'Crimson Pro' 400 with italic for sub-names; catalogue numbers and specs 'Martian Mono' 300 small caps style.
signature: Collector's loupe: holding Shift (or tapping a magnifier toggle on touch) turns the cursor into a 180px circular lens. The lens is a fixed div showing the hovered image as a background at 2.5x scale, with background-position computed from pointer offsets inside the image, a thin brass ring and a crosshair. Over text, the lens enlarges the specimen label instead, using a cloned node scaled with transform. The lens eases toward the pointer with lerp(0.18) so it feels like a physical glass.
source: Natural-history taxonomy plates and specimen drawers

name: Cross-Stitch Loom
brief: The page is an embroidered sampler on even-weave linen: a fine CSS grid texture of tiny squares underlies everything. Sections are separated by woven border bands, repeating folk motifs drawn as pixel patterns in SVG and coloured with --c-primary and --c-accent, so any brand colour becomes the thread. The hero is a framed sampler, with the headline stitched in X-stitches above an alphabet row and the year of founding, and the CTA is a stitched ribbon. Product cards sit in hoop or square frames with a running-stitch dashed border and a small stitched initial. Contact is a sampler signature block. The mood is warm, handmade and playful, softened with off-white linen and a cotton-thread sheen on hover.
type: Display: 'Yeseva One' 400 for headings and the stitched-word source; body 'Mulish' 400/700; small motif captions in 'Mulish' 800 caps, letterspaced.
signature: Self-stitching headline: the headline is rasterised to an offscreen canvas, sampled on a 10px grid, and each filled cell becomes an X stitch drawn on a visible canvas. Stitches are sewn in serpentine row order, about 600 per second, each as two diagonal strokes with a slight random angle jitter and a thread-highlight gradient. Afterwards, the pointer within 60px makes nearby stitches loosen (offset by a spring) and settle back. Card borders use the same stitch renderer to 'unpick' and re-sew on hover.
source: Folk embroidery samplers and woven textile bands

name: Dieline Pack
brief: The homepage is an unfolded carton laid flat. Sections are panels separated by dashed fold lines and dotted cut lines with tiny scissor marks, with glue tabs and registration crosses in the margins. The hero is the carton's front face: a big product name and claim, a 'net weight' badge, and a corner with a barcode generated in CSS that doubles as the CTA. Products are mini cartons on a crisp grid; their specs sit in a strict nutrition-facts-style table (heavy rules, bold numbers) for origin, size, bulk pricing and lead time, which suits B2B. Colour bars and printer's swatches in --c-primary and --c-accent sit along the trim edge. The mood is clean, light and industrial-honest.
type: Display: 'Sora' 800 tight for carton fronts and big numbers; body 'Rethink Sans' 400/700; spec tables in 'Rethink Sans' 800 for figures with heavy 8px/4px rules.
signature: Fold-up cartons: each product card is a flat net of six panels absolutely positioned with CSS 3D transforms (transform-style: preserve-3d, hinge transform-origin on each panel edge). On hover or focus, the panels fold up in sequence with a staggered GSAP timeline into a rotating box. Click spins the box 180° to show the back panel with the spec table, and Escape unfolds it flat again. On touch, a tap toggles fold/unfold, and reduced-motion users get an instant front/back flip.
source: Packaging dielines, fold diagrams and nutrition-facts panels

name: Wayfinding System
brief: The site works as a building's signage system. The header is a directory board listing zones (A Rooms / Shop, B Dining / Catalog, C Contact) with arrows and walking-time estimates. Every section is a big sign panel in --c-primary with reversed white type, a zone letter in a circle and a pictogram built from simple SVG geometry. Under it, content sits on calm light-grey 'wall' areas. The hero is one huge directional sign with an arrow and the headline as the destination, and the CTA is the 'You are here' marker. Products are sign-style tiles in a strict modular grid with level and zone codes, plus a legible info strip for price and availability. The mood is severe, bold and highly legible, with strong contrast enforced by computing white or black text against the brand colour.
type: Display: 'Overpass' 900 for signage at very large sizes with generous tracking at small sizes; body 'Overpass' 400; zone codes, distances and prices 'Overpass Mono' 600.
signature: Pointing arrows: every directional arrow (in the hero, section signs and the directory) continuously rotates to point at its target. On idle, the target is the next section's anchor; while the pointer is over the directory, the target is the hovered zone's section. The angle is computed with Math.atan2 from each arrow's bounding-box centre and eased with a critically damped spring. Hovering a directory entry also draws a temporary dashed route line (SVG polyline with right-angle segments) from the board to that section's sign.
source: Airport and hospital directional signage systems

name: Marbled Endpapers
brief: The site opens like a finely bound book. The hero is a full-bleed marbled endpaper in --c-primary, --c-accent and two derived tints, with a cream bookplate centred on it that holds the brand name, a one-line promise and the CTA. Below it, the page becomes a quiet text block with wide margins, folio numbers and running heads. Products sit in a 'tipped-in plates' grid: each card is a cream plate with a thin ruled border, a marbled corner swatch and a small caption like a bound-in illustration. Section breaks are narrow marbled bands that act as a book's edge decoration, and the contact section is an imprint/colophon page. The mood is calm, warm and tactile, with paper grain from an SVG feTurbulence filter at low opacity.
type: Display: 'Italiana' 400 at very large sizes for bookplate titles and running heads, with letterspaced small caps for folios; body 'Spectral' 300/400 with italic for captions and prices set as old-style figures.
signature: Live mathematical marbling: a canvas keeps a list of ink drops, each stored as a polygon of about 120 vertices. On load, 5–7 drops are 'floated' in brand tints using the drop transform: each existing vertex p moves to c + (p−c)·sqrt(1 + r²/|p−c|²). Dragging the pointer applies a tine-line transform to every vertex: displacement = z·u^(|d|) along the drag direction, where d is the distance to the drag line and z/u are constants, so the pattern combs and feathers exactly like a marbling stylus. Clicking drops a new ink circle at the pointer. Polygons are refilled each frame only while interacting. A 'Reset bath' button and prefers-reduced-motion both render one pre-combed static pattern.
source: Bookbinding: hand-marbled endpapers and the floating-ink bath of paper marbling

name: Signal Hoist
brief: The page is a bright, windy harbour signal mast. A tall vertical halyard line runs down the left edge with a hoist of geometric flags, one flag per section, which serve as the main navigation. The hero is a giant, crisp headline across sky-white space, with a string of code flags spelling the brand's initials flying above it, built from simple quartered, striped and crossed patterns in --c-primary, --c-accent, black and white. Products are shown as 'pennant cards': rectangular cards with a swallow-tail notch cut by clip-path and a hoist number in the corner, laid out in a staggered three-column grid. Spec rows use semaphore-style pictograms drawn in SVG. The mood is loud, sunny and athletic, with lots of white and hard geometric colour.
type: Display: 'Saira Extra Condensed' 800 uppercase, very tall, with hoist numbers set in 'Saira Extra Condensed' 300; body 'Public Sans' 400/600.
signature: Cloth-simulated flags: each flag is a canvas mesh of about 14×9 Verlet particles, pinned along its hoist edge, with distance constraints solved 3 times per frame and gravity plus a wind vector. The wind is a gentle noise breeze, increased by pointer speed (the pointer's velocity is added to the wind as it passes) and by scroll velocity. Each quad is drawn with the flag's pattern as a texture, with shading from the cross product of its normal for fold highlights. Clicking a flag on the halyard 'runs it up' to the top of the mast (a tweened y on the pin points) and scrolls to that section. Under prefers-reduced-motion the flags render flat and still.
source: Maritime signal flags and the international code of flag hoists on a ship's halyard

name: Card Catalogue
brief: The homepage is a wall of small oak-toned drawers, each with a brass label holder showing a category name in typed letters. The hero is a single large drawer pulled open, with the headline typed on a guide card and the CTA on a raised tab. The catalogue page is one open drawer: products are typed index cards with a punched rod hole, a call number (SKU), a ruled heading, a typewritten description and price, and pencil-style marginalia for stock notes. Category filters are tabbed guide cards in --c-primary that sit between the cards. Contact is a 'request slip' form on cheap pink-buff paper. The mood is studious, calm and orderly, with cream card stock, faint ruled lines and wood shading built from CSS gradients.
type: Display: 'Special Elite' for typed card headings and drawer labels; body 'Literata' 400/600 for longer reading; call numbers in 'Literata' 700 small caps with tabular figures.
signature: Flip-through drawer: the product list is a stack of absolutely positioned cards in a perspective container, each rotated around its bottom edge (rotateX) according to its distance from a 'current index' value. Wheel, drag and arrow keys change the target index, and a spring smooths the current index toward it, so cards fan forward and fall back like real index cards under a thumb. The front card stands upright and is fully interactive; cards in front of it lie flat toward the viewer and cards behind it lean back. Clicking a guide tab springs the index to that category's first card. Under prefers-reduced-motion it falls back to a plain vertical list of cards.
source: Library card catalogues: oak drawer cabinets, typed index cards, guide cards with tabs

name: Till Roll
brief: The whole page is a long, narrow strip of thermal paper running down the centre of a muted counter-top background, with the brand name in a bold header block printed at the top. The hero is printed as a receipt header: store name, address, a big dot-matrix headline, a barcode-style divider and the CTA set as a 'TOTAL' line. Sections are separated by dashed tear lines and '* * *' rows, and products are listed as line items with quantity, name, dotted leaders and price, each expandable into a mini-card with a pixel-dithered SVG illustration. A docked cart on the right edge is a second, shorter receipt. Light, dry and a little funny: the paper's slight curl, faded print edges and an occasional --c-primary stamp keep it warm.
type: Display: 'DotGothic16' for headers, totals and big numbers, set wide with a printed-dot feel; body 'Red Hat Text' 400/500 for descriptions; line items in 'Red Hat Mono' 500 for perfect column alignment.
signature: Printing and tearing the cart receipt: adding a product makes the cart receipt 'print' a new line from a slot at the top. The paper grows downward with a stepped height animation in 12px increments that mimics stepper-motor jerks, and the line's characters appear left-to-right in quick bursts. The receipt can be torn off by dragging its bottom edge sideways: a pointer drag past 80px across triggers a jagged clip-path tear (a random zigzag polygon), and the torn piece falls with rotation and gravity before the checkout panel opens. Keyboard users get a 'Tear off and check out' button that runs the same animation. The cart is stored in localStorage.
source: Thermal till receipts and shop-counter receipt printers

name: Flight Deck
brief: A dark, matte instrument panel fills the screen. The hero is a cluster of round gauges set into a riveted panel, with the headline on a placard strip above them and the CTA as a guarded toggle switch that lifts its cover on hover. Product cards are individual instruments: each one has a circular bezel framing an SVG product illustration, an outer scale that shows key specs (range, weight, power) as needle positions, and a placard label under it. Section headings are amber-style annunciator lights tinted with --c-primary that switch on as you reach them. Dark, loud and precise: brushed graphite surfaces, screw heads, and crisp white scale ticks hold up against any brand colour.
type: Display: 'Michroma' for placards and section titles, wide and small-caps style; body 'Exo 2' 400/600; gauge numerals in 'Exo 2' 700 with tabular figures.
signature: Live instruments driven by springs: every gauge needle is an SVG line whose angle follows a critically damped spring toward a target value. On the homepage, one gauge reads scroll velocity, one reads page progress, and an artificial horizon tilts with the pointer's x/y offset from the centre (pitch and roll clamped to ±15°). In the catalogue, choosing a filter or sorting sets every product's needles to that spec, so all instruments sweep to new readings at once with slight overshoot. Hovering a product makes its bezel glow in --c-primary and the needle trembles with a small noise term. Under prefers-reduced-motion the needles snap directly to their values.
source: Analogue aircraft instrument panels: round gauges, bezels, warning annunciators

name: Azulejo Wall
brief: The page is a sunlit tiled facade. The background is a grid of square tiles with procedurally generated SVG ornaments (rosettes, quatrefoils, corner arcs) drawn in --c-primary on a glazed off-white, so any brand colour reads as cobalt-like glaze. The hero is a large tile panel framed by a border of edge tiles, with the headline set as a painted cartouche in the middle. Products sit on tiles too: each card is a 2×2 tile block that shows ornament on its face and the product on its back. Section dividers are single rows of border tiles, and the contact block is a painted house-number plaque. The mood is bright, warm and decorative, with glaze highlights from radial gradients and slightly uneven hand-set grout lines.
type: Display: 'Rozha One' for headings and the painted cartouche; body 'Albert Sans' 400/600; tile captions and prices in 'Albert Sans' 800 caps.
signature: Ripple flip across the tiles: the wall is a grid of tile elements with a matching height field in a Float32Array. Clicking (or pressing Enter on) a tile injects an impulse there, and a discrete 2D wave equation (next = 2·cur − prev + c²·laplacian, damped by 0.96) spreads the disturbance. Each frame, every tile's rotateY is set from its local wave height, so a ring of tiles visibly tilts outward. Tiles whose height crosses a threshold flip 180° to swap face (ornament ↔ product), so a click in the catalogue 'turns over' a neighbourhood of tiles to reveal the products. The simulation sleeps when the energy falls below an epsilon. Under prefers-reduced-motion, only the clicked tile flips.
source: Hand-painted glazed ceramic wall tiles from Iberian building facades

name: Zoetrope Reel
brief: A playful, dark parlour with a single warm lamp. The hero is a slotted drum seen at an angle: through its black slits you glimpse a looping animation strip of the brand's mark or a simple product silhouette, with the headline arching above it like a toy's printed lid. Products are presented as animation strips: each card shows a 12-frame filmstrip of the product drawn as a generated SVG (tilting, bouncing, opening) with a sprocket-hole border, and the strip comes alive on hover. Section titles sit on round paper discs with radial frame divisions. Paper textures, gold-ink rules and --c-primary as the strip's background colour keep the toy-box mood while staying usable.
type: Display: 'Limelight' for lid titles and section discs; body 'Spline Sans' 400/500; frame numbers and prices in 'Spline Sans Mono' 500.
signature: Scroll-wound zoetrope: the hero drum is a CSS 3D cylinder of 12 slot panels (rotateY(i·30deg) translateZ(r)) with the animation frames on its inner face. Its angular velocity comes from scroll velocity, plus a flick when you drag it, decaying with friction. A slit-shutter stroboscope effect is simulated: when angular velocity is above a threshold, the visible frame is selected by floor(angle / 30°) and shown in a single fixed viewing window, so the toy appears to 'animate' at speed and blur back to separate frames as it slows down. A small speed dial shows the current fps. Product cards reuse the effect in 2D, scrubbing frames with the pointer's x. Under prefers-reduced-motion, frames are shown side by side as a static strip.
source: Pre-cinema optical toys: zoetrope drums, slit shutters and phenakistoscope discs

name: Escapement
brief: The page is the open back of a watch movement, severe and exact. A deep anthracite plate with fine Geneva-stripe gradients and perlage circles (CSS repeating radial gradients) runs behind everything, and --c-primary appears only as polished screw heads, jewel highlights and active states. The hero is a large SVG gear train that interlocks across the full width, with the headline engraved on a bridge plate and the CTA as a crown you can 'wind'. Products sit on the arbors of the gears as circular cards, and the catalogue lays them out on a grid of bridges with engraved calibre numbers. The mood is silent, technical and premium, with hairline rules, engraving-style type and generous dark space.
type: Display: 'Marcellus' with wide tracking for engraved bridge titles; body 'Questrial' 400; calibre numbers, prices and specs in 'Tenor Sans' small with tabular spacing.
signature: A meshed gear train driven by scroll: the hero and section dividers are SVG gears with real tooth counts. A single 'drive angle' comes from scroll position, and each gear's rotation is computed through the train with correct ratios (θ_next = −θ·teeth_a/teeth_b), so every gear turns in true mesh with no visible slipping. An escapement wheel and pallet fork step the seconds wheel in 6° ticks with a short ease-out, giving a mechanical tick even while scrolling smoothly. Dragging the crown in the hero winds the train and stores energy that runs it for a few seconds after release. Hovering a product gear stops the train and lifts that gear's card forward. Under prefers-reduced-motion the gears stay still and only the seconds hand ticks.
source: Mechanical watchmaking: gear trains, jewelled bridges, the tick of an escapement
